ambiguities.description: Severity and priority are described as mandatory and single-valued on 'every declared incident', but the facilitator's initial read-back said 'every incident' which Nadia corrected. Are severity/priority also mandatory only for declared incidents (like commander), or are they mandatory from creation/triage? Text says 'Every declared incident has a severity... you can't declare without one' implying triage incidents may lack severity/priority too.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Every declared incident has a severity. That's mandatory, you can't declare without one.
Owen: Priority too. Support sets it, and it's on every incident.

ambiguities.description: Does Ticket (customer report) have its own independent lifecycle/attributes, or is it purely an identifier link to an incident? The model only captures ticket number and the origin link; no other ticket attributes or states were discussed.

source_references.excerpt: Owen: And a ticket has a ticket number. Different system, different format, always has.

ambiguities.description: Severity and priority change over time and history is kept in a 'timeline' of events, but the timeline/event concept itself is not modeled as an object type since no identifier or structure was given for it. Should 'Timeline Event' be modeled as an entity capturing severity/priority history?

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: In the timeline, as events. The incident record carries the current severity.

ambiguities.description: The 'monitoring' status mentioned by Owen is explicitly rejected as a real state by Nadia ('It's not in the dropdown'). Confirmed out of scope per facilitator's ruling, but flagged here to document the decision was contentious.

source_references.excerpt: Owen: There's also "monitoring," which sits between mitigated and resolved. ... Nadia: It's not in the dropdown. ... Facilitator: If it's not in the system I'm not modelling it. Five states.

ambiguities.description: Classification of customer-caused incidents (reliability event vs. support conversation) is explicitly parked/undecided and not modeled. This is a known open item pending decision by Ravi, not an oversight, but flagged since it may need modeling later.

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: Parking it explicitly, then. Whether an incident later found to be caused by customer misconfiguration should be reclassified, excluded from reliability metrics, or left as-is, is undecided.

ambiguities.description: The duplicate-of relationship is intended to be a direct pointer to a primary (no chains), but this is not enforced in the system today. Should the acyclic/intransitive ring constraint be modeled as a hard constraint despite known violations (existing 2-deep chains)?

source_references.excerpt: Kit: It shouldn't. The intent is that everything points at the primary directly. But nothing stops you making a chain and I've seen two-deep ones. ... Kit: That's the rule as intended. It's not enforced.

ambiguities.description: Reference mode for Incident is stated as 'INC-' prefix plus a sequence -- treated here as a single simple identifier 'incident_number', but the exact format/generation scheme (prefix + sequence) is not fully specified.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Incident number. INC-, then a sequence.

object_types.name: Incident
object_types.definition: An event tracked by the organization representing a real or suspected service disruption, from triage through closure.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Incident number. INC-, then a sequence.

object_types.name: IncidentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier of an incident, formatted as INC- plus a sequence.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Incident number. INC-, then a sequence.

object_types.name: Alert
object_types.definition: A notification from the monitoring platform (or a manually raised equivalent) indicating a potential incident.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Alert ID. Comes from the monitoring platform.

object_types.name: AlertId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier of an alert, issued by the monitoring platform.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Alert ID. Comes from the monitoring platform.

object_types.name: Ticket
object_types.definition: A customer support ticket that may be linked to an incident as its origin.

source_references.excerpt: Owen: And a ticket has a ticket number. Different system, different format, always has.

object_types.name: TicketNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier of a support ticket, from the ticketing system.

source_references.excerpt: Owen: And a ticket has a ticket number. Different system, different format, always has.

object_types.name: Service
object_types.definition: A service in the catalogue that can be affected by an incident and is owned by a team.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Service name. They're unique, we enforce it in the catalogue.

object_types.name: ServiceName
object_types.definition: The unique name of a service, enforced in the service catalogue.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: Service name. They're unique, we enforce it in the catalogue.

object_types.name: Team
object_types.definition: A team that owns one or more services; the standing service owner, distinct from an incident commander.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: A team. Services are owned by teams. People move.

object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: An individual who can be assigned as an incident commander for the duration of an incident.

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: The incident commander. One person, named, and it's a role for the duration, not a job title.

object_types.name: Severity
object_types.definition: A classification of blast radius and technical impact, ranging from SEV1 (everything down for everyone) to SEV4 (degraded, cosmetic, one region).

source_references.excerpt: Nadia: SEV1 through SEV4. It's about blast radius and technical impact. SEV1 is everything's down for everyone. SEV4 is degraded, cosmetic, one region, nobody's really suffering.

object_types.name: Priority
object_types.definition: A classification of customer urgency and commercial impact, ranging from P1 to P4, set by support and independent of severity.

source_references.excerpt: Owen: And priority is P1 through P4. ... Priority is about customer urgency. Who's affected, what they've promised their own customers, whether we're breaching an SLA.

object_types.name: IncidentState
object_types.definition: The current lifecycle state of an incident.
